title: Novel TPMS Metamaterial Generation + Multi-Physics Simulation
description: Pipeline that generates genuinely novel triply-periodic minimal surfaces by sampling random points in a 12-dimensional Fourier basis, then drives them to zero mean curvature. Runs nonlinear FEA compression, transient heat conduction, and Darcy flow on each generated structure.
details: Built a generative pipeline for novel TPMS metamaterials in pure Python - every known TPMS (Gyroid, Schwarz P, Diamond, I-WP, Neovius) is a specific point in a 12-dimensional Fourier basis of cubic-symmetric periodic functions; random coefficients produce surfaces that don't match any known TPMS.
Drives each candidate toward H = 0 (the mathematical definition of a minimal surface) via iterative mean curvature flow with numerical convergence checking.
Marching cubes contouring on a high-resolution voxel grid followed by Laplacian smoothing produces watertight, 3D-printable STL meshes.
Hand-rolled nonlinear FEA: Total Lagrangian formulation, Saint Venant-Kirchhoff hyperelastic material, Newton-Raphson over 15 load increments to 30% strain. No external FEA library.

Multi-physics analysis on each generated structure: transient heat conduction (implicit FDM, heterogeneous solid/void conductivity) and pressure-driven creeping flow through the void network (Darcy regime).
Per-geometry outputs: STL mesh, compression animation, mean-curvature heatmap, thermal/flow dashboards, force-displacement CSV.
By tuning wall thickness and which basis functions are active, stiffness can be dialed in precisely - at the right settings, TPMS lattices can be more efficient impact padding than conventional foam.

title: 2D/3D CFD of MacBook Pro 16-inch Thermal Management
description: Two coupled Navier-Stokes + energy CFD solvers (2D and 3D) that predict the thermal field of a 16-inch MacBook Pro chassis under sustained CPU load. Validated against five independent published thermal reviews.
details: Built two finite-volume CFD solvers from scratch in Python (2D top-down and full 3D) to predict the thermal field of a 16-inch MacBook Pro chassis under sustained CPU load.
Used a staggered MAC grid, pseudo-transient Chorin projection with implicit Brinkman penalization, and direct sparse LU factorization of the pressure-correction Poisson equation via SciPy's splu.
2D model: 260x180 grid (18,875 flow cells) with a 1D out-of-plane closure and algebraic mixing-length turbulence model.
3D model: 90x62x16 grid (49,662 flow cells) resolving the vertical dimension directly, with an explicit thermal-interface-material layer above the SoC die.
Monitored convergence via two independent residuals - L-infinity divergence on deep interior flow cells reached ~1e-13 (2D) and ~1e-11 (3D).
Three-level grid refinement study (130x90, 260x180, 520x360) gives GCI <= 1.7% for battery, palm-rest, and exhaust metrics.
Predicted SoC temperatures: 96 C (2D) and 81 C (3D); published range from five independent reviews is 82-98 C.
2D/3D spread is attributable to the 6x larger heat-loss surface area resolved in 3D plus the explicit TIM resistance.

title: Helical Compression Spring Design Optimization
description: Minimum-mass spring optimization using fmincon under 7 constraints including stress, surge frequency, and buckling. Material: ASTM A228 music wire.
details: Formulated the minimum-mass design of a helical compression spring as a constrained nonlinear program in three variables: wire diameter, mean coil diameter, and active coil count.

Enforced seven inequality constraints: Wahl-corrected shear stress (Zimmerli criterion), coil-bind clearance, spring-index manufacturability bounds, minimum deflection stroke, surge-frequency margin (13x operating frequency), and Euler-column buckling stability.
Solved with MATLAB's fmincon interior-point algorithm from eight Latin-hypercube starting points.
Independently validated by a 40x40 brute-force parametric sweep across the design space.
Both methods converged to the same optimum: d = 2.965 mm, D = 12.665 mm, Na = 7.77 coils - mass = 21.1 g with a stress safety factor of exactly 1.00.
Sensitivity analysis identified allowable shear stress as the dominant driver - a 10% relaxation of the stress limit reduces optimal mass by ~18%.

title: 2D CPU/GPU Die Thermal Simulation
description: 2D heat transfer simulation of a CPU/GPU chip stack using explicit, implicit, and steady-state finite difference solvers.
details: Implemented a 2D transient and steady-state thermal simulation of a multi-layer CPU/GPU chip package (20 mm x 6 mm cross-section) in MATLAB using finite difference methods.
Domain models three physical layers - silicon die, thermal interface material (TIM), and copper heat spreader - with three localized volumetric heat sources representing CPU cores.
Built and compared three solvers: explicit forward-time central-space (FTCS), implicit backward-time central-space (BTCS) solved via Gauss-Seidel, and a direct steady-state Gauss-Seidel solver.
Peak junction temperatures reached 380-420 K depending on core position; the center core runs hottest due to reduced lateral conduction.
Identified the TIM layer as the dominant thermal resistance and confirmed the copper heat spreader's role in laterally redistributing heat and reducing hotspot temperatures.
All three solvers converge to the same steady-state distribution, validating the numerical implementation.

title: Detecting Faulty PCBs Using Thermal Image Analysis
description: 97% accuracy detecting faulty connections on PCBs using thermal image processing
details: Built a MATLAB image processing pipeline that detects faulty solder joints on printed circuit boards from thermal camera images.

Generated synthetic thermal PCB images as grids of circular pads with controlled defect injection - defective pads assigned higher intensity to simulate excess heat from short circuits or degraded components, with additive Gaussian noise for realism.
Preprocessed each image with grayscale conversion and Gaussian blur, then applied intensity thresholding (threshold = 0.8) to segment hotspot regions.
Extracted connected regions and characterized them by centroid location and area.
Auto-generates timestamped multi-page PDF reports with side-by-side raw and annotated thermal images per board, plus CSV summaries for downstream analysis.
Achieved 97% detection accuracy on the synthetic dataset.

title: Apple iPod Design Challenge
description: Two competing CAD design concepts for an Apple iPod redesign, with full assemblies, schematics, and DFM analysis.
details: Designed two competing battery-door release mechanisms for the Classic iPod in SolidWorks.
Design 1 - elastic bending arms: a button press deflects integrated cantilever beams downward, disengaging retention features to release the door.

Design 2 - inclined-surface (wedge) mechanism: a button press drives clasps laterally outward via a 50-degree wedge, converting vertical motion into horizontal displacement that lifts the battery door.
Ran a pro/con trade study across durability, cycle life, and manufacturing; selected Design 2 for its controlled, repeatable actuation and resistance to creep and fatigue.
Produced full CAD assemblies, section views, exploded views, and component-level FEA (von Mises stress under extreme loads with safety factors from 2.1 to 13.7).
Included a detailed bill of materials with unit cost estimates and button ergonomics sized to DoD design criteria; all parts injection-molded PC or ABS.

title: Voice Controlled Robotic Arm Assistant
description: Custom robotic arm with AI companion with speech recognition
details: Designed and built a custom robotic arm with integrated voice control using speech recognition and machine learning.
Modeled the mechanical design in CAD with FEA validation of joint loads and deflection under payload.
Built a control system that translates spoken commands into servo movements through a trained speech-to-intent model.
Enables hands-free operation for pick-and-place tasks.

title: TPMS for Headgear Impact Protection
description: Developing headgear with TPMS structures to improve shear protection with improved strength to weight efficiency
details: Researching Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) lattice structures - gyroid and Schwarz-P - as energy-absorbing liners in protective headgear.
TPMS geometries offer superior strength-to-weight ratios compared to traditional EPS foam.
Using CAD modeling and FEA to evaluate how TPMS unit cell type, relative density, and wall thickness affect impact energy absorption and shear force transmission.
Goal: develop a liner that reduces rotational acceleration during oblique impacts, improving protection against concussive injuries.

title: Personal Productivity, Fitness, and Goals App
description: IOS app to track daily productivity, fitness, and goals with SwiftUI
details: Built a personal productivity desktop application for tracking daily habits across productivity, fitness, and personal goals.
Runs fully offline - all data saved locally as a JSON file that survives app updates and reboots.
Features a dashboard for daily progress, streak monitoring, and customizable goal categories.
Designed to build consistent routines through visual progress feedback, without any cloud services or accounts.

title: Modeling Equity Option Performance
description: Options hit probabilities and expected payoff timing calculator
details: Built a Python GUI application for evaluating equity options contracts.
Computes Black-Scholes theoretical fair value for calls and puts.
Runs Monte Carlo price path simulations to estimate the probability of hitting a user-defined take-profit threshold and the average time to reach it.
Smart verdict system compares the option's bid-ask midpoint against theoretical value to classify contracts as undervalued, fairly priced, or overvalued.
Integrates live market data from Yahoo Finance API to auto-fill spot price, dividend yield, and implied volatility.
Full pipeline: user input -> market data fetch -> pricing engine -> Monte Carlo simulation -> Greek calculation -> valuation verdict, displayed in a Tkinter interface.
